pool.text: A diagnostic test produces false negatives with probability 0.05 and false positives with probability 0.08. If 10% of the tested population actually has the condition, what is the probability that a randomly tested person receives a positive test result?
pool.sol: True positive rate = \( 1 - 0.05 = 0.95 \). Population with disease = 10%. False positive rate = 0.08. Population without disease = 90%. Total positive rate = \( (0.10 \times 0.95) + (0.90 \times 0.08) = 0.095 + 0.072 = 0.167 \).

pool.sol: The numbers greater than 4 on a standard die are 5 and 6 (2 outcomes out of 6). The probability is \( \dfrac{2}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3} \approx 0.33 \). (Accept 1/3 or 0.33).

pool.text: A card is drawn from a standard deck of 52 cards. Given that the card is a red card, what is the probability that it is an ace?
pool.sol: There are 26 red cards in a standard deck (hearts and diamonds). Exactly 2 of these red cards are aces (Ace of hearts, Ace of diamonds). Conditional probability = \( \dfrac{2}{26} = \dfrac{1}{13} \approx 0.077 \). (Accept 1/13 or 0.077).
